principle: Gates are never lowered to hit the publishing schedule. A failing item is quarantined with a logged reason and Agent 0 selects the next candidate instead.

checks: No political figures, parties, elections, or policy debate
No claims presented as fact that cannot be sourced from the script's own generic motivational framing (no fabricated statistics, studies, or quotes attributed to real named individuals)
No controversial social topics (per config/channel.json content_exclusions)
factual_controversy_screen.on_fail: quarantine; log matched phrase/topic; return to Agent 0 for a new candidate

checks: No hate speech, harassment, or targeting of protected groups
No graphic violence, self-harm, or dangerous-act depictions
No misleading titles/thumbnails not supported by video content (no clickbait mismatch)
Complies with YouTube monetization + reused-content policies at a basic level (not purely static/looping with zero transformation for shorts)
Output resolution matches target (1080x1920 shorts, 1920x1080 or native long-form)
Duration within target range for the format
basic_qa.on_fail: quarantine; log which QA check failed; do not retry-publish without regenerating

copyright_gate.status: intentionally not automated for short-form source clips
copyright_gate.rationale: Channel owner explicitly accepted the risk of reusing third-party sourced clips (see assets/short-form-clips/raw/README.md), on condition that Agent 3.1 transforms every clip (reframe/crop, speed or color change, swapped-in audio) before publish. This is a documented decision, not a silent skip. Note: the caption/text-overlay requirement below was REMOVED 2026-07-27 per owner direction — captions are dropped entirely now, see agents/short_form/3.1_producer.md.
mitigation_required_before_publish: at least one of: speed change, color grade change
original audio replaced with a track from state/cc0_audio_library.json OR state/trending_audio_library.json
copyright_gate.backstop: YouTube Content ID is the real enforcement mechanism; expect possible revenue-share claims. Channel owner has accepted this.

audio_license_gate.status: CC0-only requirement explicitly LIFTED for short-form audio as of 2026-07-27, channel owner's direct decision — real trending/copyrighted commercial songs are now permitted, sourced via state/trending_audio_library.json.
audio_license_gate.rationale: Owner was told plainly that this is a materially different risk than the video-clip reuse decision above: these are named, signed-artist commercial songs (CKay, Indila, Ice Spice, FloyyMenor, Brazilian phonk/montagem producers, etc.), not obscure unidentifiable reposts — Content ID match is near-certain, not just possible. Presented three options (use real songs / stay CC0-only / CC0-styled middle ground); owner chose to use the real songs anyway, explicitly accepting the risk. This is a deliberate, informed decision, not an oversight or a silent policy drift.
checks: Track is either in state/cc0_audio_library.json (verified CC0) OR in state/trending_audio_library.json (real song, sourced with documented provenance)

If from trending_audio_library.json: source URL/video the audio was pulled from is recorded, and the track is genuinely identified (a real song/artist name, not a generic 'original sound' repost label) — see state/performance_notes.json's TikTok scan honesty notes for what counts as genuinely identified
audio_license_gate.backstop: Content ID will likely mute/claim revenue on these tracks, and repeated copyright strikes risk channel termination under YouTube's 3-strike policy. Channel owner has explicitly accepted this, understanding it is a materially higher risk than the video-clip mitigation above. Monitor state/quarantine.json and actual channel strikes/claims — if real strikes start accumulating, revisit this decision with the owner rather than continuing by default.

image_copyright_gate.status: As of 2026-07-27, a second accepted path exists alongside AI generation: owner-supplied images of unverified/unknown provenance, explicitly risk-accepted by the channel owner. See rationale below before assuming either path is the default.
checks_path_a_ai_generated: Background image was generated (Nano Banana / AI image gen), not scraped or copied from another creator's work
checks_path_b_owner_supplied: Image is listed in state/image_pool.json with source: 'owner_provided_unverified' (legacy folder) or 'owner_ai_generated_from_reference' (active folder as of 2026-07-28)
The specific owner-supplied risk_acceptance note (see below) is referenced, not re-litigated per video
image_copyright_gate.rationale_path_b: Owner supplied a Google Drive folder of luxury car/mansion images (folder id 1eDQ9-NyZ1ko8WTmaNSDtrNwQUFuQI24g) for a new long-form loop format. On inspection, the images carry real provenance red flags: generic browser 'download (N).jpg' filenames indicating they were pulled from the web rather than owned/created by the channel owner, and one file's original filename was a Russian-language Bitcoin-wallet ad title, suggesting at least one image originated from a crypto-ad/stock page rather than a personal or licensed source. This was explicitly flagged to the owner before use. Owner's direct response: 'just try to make one video, if it gets copyrighted ill change the plan' — an informed decision to proceed despite the disclosed provenance risk, distinct from and in addition to the short-form clip-reuse and trending-audio risk acceptances already on file. SUPERSEDED 2026-07-28 for new candidates — see rationale_path_b_active below.
image_copyright_gate.rationale_path_b_active: As of 2026-07-28 the owner switched the active source to Drive folder 1ZdzOguJXaP4zxDSPVpuOTXhWGfTBOy09 (source='owner_ai_generated_from_reference'). Owner's own account: found real photos online, had ChatGPT turn each into a structured JSON scene description, then generated new images from that JSON prompt — text-to-image synthesis guided by a reference, not direct reuse/edit of the original photo. Lower risk than the legacy folder (no reused pixels from an unverified rights-holder's photo), but a residual risk was disclosed to and accepted by the owner: a sufficiently detailed prompt can still reproduce specific real elements (a legible license plate, a specific yacht's name, exact real signage) closely enough to read as a derivative of one particular real photo's composition, not a generic AI scene. Same per-file visual-check discipline as path B legacy still applies (watermarks, ad/scam text, off-theme content) — see agents/long_form/2.2_image_sourcer.md.
image_copyright_gate.on_fail: quarantine; regenerate (path A) or pull a different owner-supplied image and re-flag (path B)
image_copyright_gate.backstop: YouTube Content ID / copyright claims are the real enforcement mechanism for path B images, same as the short-form clip-reuse and trending-audio decisions. If a claim or strike actually lands on a path-B video, stop using new images from this source and revisit with the owner rather than continuing by default — per the owner's own stated condition ('if it gets copyrighted ill change the plan').
